evidence_levels.RAN: Backed by a command or search whose output I saw
evidence_levels.READ: Concluded by reading the code myself
evidence_levels.READ_SUBAGENT: Read by a sub-agent that used cat -n; line numbers come from that read
evidence_levels.INFERRED: Reasoned from code and library behaviour, not executed

tooling_limitations: The shell stopped returning output after my second command (even 'echo alive' came back empty, exit -1), and a background terminal also produced nothing. After that I used only file-read and ripgrep-based search tools.
So I could NOT run cfn-lint, python ast.parse, the babel parse or bash -n myself.

Before their shells hung, sub-agents RAN: ast.parse on all backend Python (all OK); a @babel/parser pass over 48 frontend src files (0 failures); eslint 8.57.1 (0 errors, 29 warnings); bash -n on every bash script (OK); a CR count on 46 bin/ and backend-flask/bin files (0 in every file); a simulation of migration timestamp widths; a luxon format test.
cfn-lint 1.49.3 is installed, but no lint output was obtained for any template.
Side effects outside the repo, disclosed: one sub-agent created /tmp/null_err_unused and did not delete it. Another may have written and then deleted /tmp/.cr_audit_bundle.txt.

findings.title: teardown-all destroys the RDS instance with --skip-final-snapshot, with no automatic snapshot and no check that dependent stacks were actually deleted
findings.evidence: The script has no set -e on purpose. If CrdAuth or CrdService fails to delete, it prints a message and keeps going, then runs delete-db-instance --skip-final-snapshot. A search for create-db-snapshot or final-db-snapshot across bin/, aws/cfn/ and backend-flask/bin/ found zero hits. Every deploy restores from the pinned snapshot.
findings.impact: Every teardown permanently loses everything written since the pinned snapshot (signups, cruds, replies, profile edits) unless someone takes a manual snapshot first. The instance is also deleted even when stacks that import CrdDb exports still exist.
findings.recommendation: Before the RDS delete: (1) check with describe-stacks that CrdAuth and CrdService are gone, and abort if not; (2) create a dated cruddur-crddb-* snapshot, wait for it, and print its ID for config.toml. Never delete existing snapshots.

findings.title: Direct messages have no membership check (IDOR) on read or write
locations: backend-flask/services/messages.py:13-20 (my_user_uuid is computed, then never used)
backend-flask/services/create_message.py:70-77 ('update' mode writes to any message_group_uuid the client sends)
backend-flask/lib/ddb.py:53-70 (list_messages queries MSG#<group> with no owner filter)
findings.evidence: Ddb.list_messages(ddb, message_group_uuid) runs for any authenticated caller. create_message in update mode never checks that the sender is in the group.
findings.impact: Any signed-in user who has or guesses a group UUID can read or post into another pair's private conversation. UUIDv4 values are hard to guess, which lowers the risk but does not remove it.
findings.recommendation: Before reading or writing, confirm that a GRP#<my_user_uuid> item with that message_group_uuid exists (query the GSI), and return 403 if not.

findings.title: Bearer tokens and PII are written to CloudWatch
locations: backend-flask/app.py:437 print(f'Headers: {dict(request.headers)}') logs the full Authorization header on every POST/OPTIONS to /api/activities
backend-flask/app.py:199 prints the first 50 chars of the Authorization header on every request
backend-flask/lib/db.py print_sql/print_params print the full SQL and params (message text, cognito ids) on every query (verbose=True by default)
aws/lambdas/cruddur-upload-avatar/function.rb:6 (puts event, full headers) and :24 (logs the raw access_token)
aws/lambdas/lambda-authorizer/index.js:13 logs the full event, including the authorization header
findings.evidence: Stdout goes to the awslogs driver. app.logger.debug(claims) calls (app.py:258, 281, 307, 366) are probably dropped in prod because Flask's logger defaults to WARNING; the print() calls are not.
findings.impact: Anyone with CloudWatch Logs read access can replay a still-valid access token. User PII is retained for 14 days.
findings.recommendation: Remove the header dumps and the token prints. Log request ID, path and status only. Make SQL logging opt-in.

findings.title: schema.sql doesn't match the migrations, and bin/db/setup never runs migrate
locations: backend-flask/db/schema.sql:24 reply_to_activity_uuid integer (the migration changes it to uuid)
backend-flask/db/schema.sql (no users.bio column; migration 17749981238427508_add_bio_column adds it)
backend-flask/db/schema.sql:31-39 schema_information uses CREATE IF NOT EXISTS + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
backend-flask/bin/db/setup:12-16 runs drop, create, schema-load, seed, update_cognito_user_ids (no migrate)
findings.evidence: Fresh setup: tables are created in their pre-migration shape. Profile, update and home queries fail until someone runs migrate by hand. Re-running schema-load on an existing DB is worse: tables are recreated in the old shape, schema_information survives and still claims every migration ran, so migrate silently skips them all.
findings.impact: Local and new environments break in ways that look like application bugs.
findings.recommendation: Fold all three migrations into schema.sql, or have setup run migrate. Reset schema_information whenever schema-load recreates the tables.

findings.title: The migration generator emits variable-width timestamp prefixes, so new migrations can be skipped silently
findings.evidence: Sub-agent simulation of 20,000 timestamps gave widths {17: 15215, 16: 4309, 15: 428, 14: 40, 13: 5, 12: 3}, so about 24% are shorter than 17 digits. The stored value is 17800000000000001. A 16-digit prefix is roughly 10x smaller and never runs.
findings.impact: Future schema changes never reach prod, and nothing reports it.
findings.recommendation: Generate a fixed-width prefix (for example time.time_ns() zero-padded, or a YYYYMMDDHHMMSS format that is always larger than the current stored value) and sort numerically.

findings.title: Failed DB writes are swallowed and can come back as HTTP 200
locations: backend-flask/lib/db.py:59-60 query_commit catches every Exception and only calls print_sql_err
backend-flask/lib/db.py:95-96 query_object_json returns the STRING '{}' when there is no row
backend-flask/services/create_activity.py:105-113 no None check on the returned uuid (create_reply.py has one)
findings.evidence: Any exception without pgerror (every non-psycopg exception, and probably psycopg3 errors too; not verified because psycopg isn't installed on the host) raises AttributeError inside the except block. Otherwise query_commit returns None, query_object_activity(None) matches no rows, and the route returns 200 with the text '{}'.
findings.impact: Posts can appear to succeed without being saved. The error surfaces as a misleading 500 or as nothing at all.
findings.recommendation: Log the error and re-raise in query_commit. Use err.diag / err.sqlstate for psycopg3. Return a structured error from services. Return real JSON (or None) instead of the string '{}'.

findings.title: Crud expiry (TTL) is stored but never enforced
findings.evidence: A search for 'expires_at >', 'expires_at <' or now() across backend-flask/db/** found only schema defaults and seed data (RAN). No cleanup job exists.
findings.impact: Expired cruds show forever. formatTimeExpires then renders negative values such as '-4320m' (INFERRED from the code path).
findings.recommendation: Add 'AND (activities.expires_at IS NULL OR activities.expires_at > now())' to the feed, profile and replies SQL. Optionally add a scheduled purge.

findings.title: bin/frontend/build doesn't pass REACT_APP_API_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT_URL
locations: bin/frontend/build:26-34 (5 --build-arg flags; the API gateway one is missing)
frontend-react-js/Dockerfile.prod:14, :22 (declares the ARG and ENV correctly)

findings.impact: Any image built by this script bakes an undefined gateway URL. Avatar upload then fails silently: POST to 'undefined/avatars/key_upload', presignedUrl undefined, fetch(undefined).
findings.recommendation: Add --build-arg REACT_APP_API_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT_URL. Fail the build if any required REACT_APP_* value is empty.

findings.title: Per-route @cross_origin() likely overrides the restricted CORS origin list
findings.evidence: Bare @cross_origin() uses flask-cors defaults (origins '*'). If either env var is unset, origins also contains None.
findings.impact: Most API routes probably accept any origin. Auth is a bearer header, not cookies, which limits the damage.
findings.recommendation: Remove the decorators and rely on the app-level config, or pass origins explicitly.
findings.evidence_level: READ; flask-cors precedence UNVERIFIED (library not installed on host)

findings.title: Frontend tasks share the service SG that RDS allows on 5432
findings.impact: The nginx frontend tasks have network access to the database, which isn't least privilege.
findings.recommendation: Give the frontend its own SG, or give the backend a dedicated SG and reference only that one from the DB SG.

findings.title: UserFeedPage passes incomplete props: Reply on the profile page throws, and posting from the profile throws after the save
findings.evidence: The page renders no ReplyForm. The effect doesn't re-run when params.handle changes, so navigating from /@a to /@b keeps showing the old profile.

findings.title: MessageItem links to a route that doesn't exist
findings.evidence: That URL matches /messages/:message_group_uuid with '@handle' as the uuid, so the page calls GET /api/messages/@handle and DynamoDB returns nothing.

findings.title: Dates older than 24h show the month number instead of the day
findings.evidence: In luxon, 'L' is the month number. The sub-agent's test printed 'Dec 12' for 2024-12-25; 'LLL d' gives 'Dec 25'.
findings.impact: Every timestamp older than a day is wrong in the feed, message groups and messages.
findings.recommendation: Use 'LLL d'.

findings.title: Inbox and thread queries filter by the current year, so conversations vanish on Jan 1
findings.evidence: The year comes from local time while sk is UTC ISO-8601. Limit 20, no pagination.
findings.impact: On 2027-01-01, every 2026 conversation drops out of the inbox and threads.
findings.recommendation: Drop the year condition, or use sk > a cutoff. Add pagination with LastEvaluatedKey.

findings.title: import process from 'process' in four forms changes how REACT_APP_* values resolve
findings.evidence: In the local bundle build/static/js/main.9dedd425.js (RAN search), ActivityForm compiles to wd().env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, where wd = module 285 = the npm process polyfill with r.env={}. HomeFeedPage, which has no import, gets the inlined env object instead. That local bundle was built without REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. journal/week14.md:73, :79 reports posting, DMs and avatar upload (all four affected forms) working in prod, so webpack most likely inlines the full key when the variable is defined.
findings.impact: Works in prod according to the journal, but it's fragile. Any missing variable falls through to undefined with no build-time signal. The deployed bundle couldn't be checked (DNS down).
findings.recommendation: Delete the four import lines. CRA injects process.env itself.

findings.title: Avatar upload path: PNG key mismatch, unverified JWT decode, repo authorizer not matching the header format, nothing in IaC
locations: frontend-react-js/src/components/ProfileForm.js accept='image/jpeg,image/png'; upload key keeps the file extension
aws/lambdas/process-images/index.js:25-26 keeps the extension; :44-56 sets ContentType image/jpeg without converting
